name: sadness
quote: I'm not going to get that job I really wanted.
description: An extended experience of loss and displeasure about your situation but without a sense of immediate threat. It may be triggered by an outcome that significantly degrades your life situation or just from recognizing that things are pretty bad as they are.
perceptions: An event or realization causes a sense that things are not as you they should be.
results: Sadness ranges in strength from mild to tears.

guidance.description: Sadness is a normal part of life, but that doesn’t mean it isn’t difficult to cope with feelings of sorrow and unhappiness you may be experiencing. Whether you’re struggling with disappointment or you’re feeling deep anguish, know that you’re not alone. Most importantly, know that the pain you’re feeling right now most likely won’t last forever.

comparisons.description: 'Melancholy' is an extended contemplative sadness. 'Depression' includes gloom and sadness along with many debilitating symptoms such as social withdrawal and inability to enjoy anything.

'Sadness' is about a void caused by loss or longing, while 'angst' is a general anxiety. Both can be caused by big picture concerns, but the outcome is quite different, the output of sadness is tears while the output of angst is nerves.

variations.name: sympathetic sadness
variations.description: Connecting with another person or creature's negative experience that creates a vicarious sense of loss or longing.
perceptions: I had a physical or mental interaction with another person or creature who is having a negative experience.
I share a sense of loss or longing with them.
results: Sadness ranges in strength from mild to tears.

guidance.description: It’s important we make sure we are there and present for the people in our life who need us most, of course, but can we do so while protecting our own emotional wellbeing? Absolutely.

examples: Your relative has a string of bad luck.
A baby bird fell out of its nest.

commentaries.quote: The walls we build around us to keep sadness out also keep out the joy.
If you're not sad about something at least every other week, you're either enlightened, lucky, or not engaged in life.
It's not necessary for anything to actually change to cause sadness. A simple shift in perception is enough.

The unhappy person resents it when you try to cheer him up, because that means he has to stop dwelling on himself and start paying attention to the universe. Unhappiness is the ultimate form of self-indulgence. When you're unhappy, you get to pay a lot of attention to yourself. You get to take yourself oh so very seriously.
When thunderstorms roll in, you make a choice to either succumb with tears to the gloomy downpour, or smile and look for rainbows.
